name: Feature Stack
text: Hero, then features revealed one full-width band at a time down the scroll, each an alternating text/visual split. The workhorse product page — but built as bands, not a 3-up card grid, and every band leads with a real mockup/chart, not a paragraph. When: a product with 3-6 distinct capabilities that each deserve a real visual. Mood: any; the default reach for premium/technical SaaS.

name: Bento Showcase
text: An asymmetric grid of mixed-span tiles (1×1, 2×1, 2×2) where each tile shows one capability as a small live-looking UI fragment. Visual rhythm comes from tile size, not repetition. When: a product with many small features that are more compelling shown-at-a-glance than explained in sequence. Mood: premium, technical, playful.

name: Editorial Index
text: Reads like a well-set magazine or a studio's index page: a masthead, a numbered or categorized list of work/sections, generous type, hairline rules. Content-led, not conversion-led. When: portfolios, agencies, publications, "this is who we are" pages. Mood: elegant, premium.

name: Long-Scroll Narrative
text: the narrative arc from  told top to bottom, one full-section beat at a time, with a scroll-linked reveal between them. The page is a story, not a menu — this is the macrostructure where the arc is most visually literal, but the arc itself applies to every macrostructure, not just this one. When: a non-obvious product that needs explaining before the pitch lands; a manifesto; a launch. Mood: any; strong for warm, elegant, technical.

name: Stat-Led
text: A single dominant number or a tight row of real metrics is the hero and the spine of the page; everything else supports the figures. When: the product's story is genuinely quantitative and the numbers are real (never invented — see the honesty rule below). Mood: premium, technical.

name: Gallery Grid
text: The work is the pitch: a grid of real photography, product shots, or case tiles fills the page, chrome kept minimal. When: commerce, photography, food, travel, physical product, anything where the imagery sells. Mood: elegant, warm, playful.

name: Product Demo / Workbench
text: The hero is the product in use (a real annotated mockup, an interactive-looking capture, a clipped-by-viewport demo), and the page is organized around doing, not describing. When: dev tools, apps, anything where seeing it work is the strongest argument. Mood: technical, premium.

name: Split Diptych
text: The page runs as a two-column composition — a persistent statement/nav column beside a scrolling content column, or a hard left/right split fold. When: studios, single-voice products, anything wanting an art-directed rather than stacked feel. Mood: elegant, premium, playful.

name: Conversational FAQ
text: The page is built around real questions the audience actually asks, answered directly, with proof and CTA folded into the answers. When: products fighting a specific objection or a trust gap (regulated, high-consideration, "is this legit"). Mood: warm, technical.

name: Manifesto
text: Type-forward, few images, one strong point of view carried by big statements and short lines. The restraint is the design. When: brand-led launches, opinionated products, a studio staking a position. Mood: elegant, premium, technical.

name: Catalogue
text: A structured, almost tabular listing (products, plans, specs, releases) presented with editorial care rather than as a bare table. When: commerce with many SKUs, pricing-as-page, changelogs, spec-heavy products. Mood: technical, elegant.

name: Poster Fold
text: One full-bleed art-directed fold (a photograph, a hand-built illustration, a bold type composition) carries the whole first screen; the page below becomes something quieter. When: the brand or a single image is the message — events, fashion, a hero launch moment. Mood: elegant, playful, warm.
